integrity: Both archives match the npm registry SHA-512 integrity records.

diff.summary: TLS probe and its callers are unchanged. Changes add the CI service name to existing build metadata, camelCase CLI flag declarations for meow 9, owner-qualified branch display, dependency updates, changelog entries, and Babel template caching. Source map sourcesContent is identical.

execution_trace: bin/register.js loads dotenv, initializes esm and invokes main with CLI arguments. It does not require(module).
getOptions.js derives the Storybook URL from localhost plus the configured port, or the explicit --storybook-url option.
tasks/start.js calls checkResponse; startApp launches the caller-selected npm script or --exec command and polls for readiness.
checkResponse uses a rejectUnauthorized:false HTTPS agent only for HTTPS, awaits fetch and returns a boolean. It never interprets the response body as code or sends a request body.
HTTPClient.js and uploadFiles.js implement separate authenticated build API and Storybook artifact upload paths without this permissive agent.
verify.js sends build metadata with environment names restricted by /^GERRIT/ and /^TRAVIS/; log.js sends application logs to Loggly. These paths are unchanged.
analysis: Plain JavaScript was inspected and compared across both complete archives. The tiny minified addon was checked against its unchanged embedded source. No hostile addition or concealed loader was found.
intent_correction: Removed import-plus-TLS-option co-occurrence as an evasion claim. TLS disabling remains notable; structured HTTPS agent construction is now a notable TLS initialization capability.
other_corrections: Move generic addon member references from browser-extension management to data/property/access, and remove them as evidence of extension ID comparison.
Rename generic open-event dispatch so filesystem streams are not called connections. Update the WebSocket consumer and fixture references.
Match direct identifier-argument require syntax rather than the flattened call projection, which confuses invocation of require(esm) results with dynamic module names.
limitations: Static execution-path analysis; Node.js is unavailable for a runtime harness. Analyzer reports flow limitations, so source inspection and full archive comparison supply the decisive evidence.
